Methodology: hand-computed worked examples

Source: vignettes/methodology.Rmd
methodology.Rmd

Every computation in cer is verifiable with pen and paper. This vignette walks through the three formula functions.

1. Safeguard declining baseline

Formula

Bt=EI×ERCt B_t \;=\; EI \times ERC_t

where EIEI is the default emissions intensity in Schedule 1 of the Safeguard Mechanism Rule 2015 and ERCtERC_t the default emissions reduction contribution in section 31: 0.951 for 2023-24, falling by 0.049 a year to 0.657 for 2029-30, then by 0.03285 a year.

Hand calculation

The default emissions intensity for primary aluminium (Schedule 1, section 7) is 1.94 t CO2-e per tonne. For FY 2029-30:

B2029-30=1.94×0.657=1.275 B_{2029\text{-}30} = 1.94 \times 0.657 = 1.275

Package output 

traj <- cer_safeguard_baseline_trajectory("Aluminium",
                                           from_year = 2023,
                                           to_year = 2029)
traj
#>   year financial_year default_emissions_intensity decline_factor baseline
#> 1 2023        2023-24                        1.94          0.951  1.84494
#> 2 2024        2024-25                        1.94          0.902  1.74988
#> 3 2025        2025-26                        1.94          0.853  1.65482
#> 4 2026        2026-27                        1.94          0.804  1.55976
#> 5 2027        2027-28                        1.94          0.755  1.46470
#> 6 2028        2028-29                        1.94          0.706  1.36964
#> 7 2029        2029-30                        1.94          0.657  1.27458

Row for 2029: baseline = 1.275. Matches.

Sanity check at the first year 

traj[traj$year == 2023, ]
#>   year financial_year default_emissions_intensity decline_factor baseline
#> 1 2023        2023-24                        1.94          0.951  1.84494

ERC = 0.951; baseline = 1.94 x 0.951 = 1.845. The decline is linear in the ERC, not compounded: a geometric 4.9 per cent a year would give 0.740 rather than 0.657 by 2029-30.

2. QCMR reconciliation

Formula

π=V−RR \pi \;=\; \frac{V - R}{R}

where V is the live-fetched aggregate and R the QCMR reference.

Hand calculation

ACCU cumulative issuances at end of 2024-Q4 per the QCMR data workbook = 159,125,069. Suppose a user’s fetch shows 158,400,000 (0.46 per cent low).

π=158,400,000−159,125,069159,125,069=−725,069159,125,069=−0.00456=−0.456% \pi = \frac{158{,}400{,}000 - 159{,}125{,}069}{159{,}125{,}069} = \frac{-725{,}069}{159{,}125{,}069} = -0.00456 = -0.456\%

Package output 

cer_reconcile(value   = 158400000,
              quarter = "2024-Q4",
              measure = "accu_cumulative_issuances")
#>                     measure quarter     value reference    diff     pct_diff
#> 1 accu_cumulative_issuances 2024-Q4 158400000 159125069 -725069 -0.004556598
#>    unit                                                                  source
#> 1 accus QCMR data workbook (september-quarter-2026), Figure 1.2, column 'Total'

At -0.46 per cent the reconciliation falls within the default 2 per cent warning threshold; no warning fires.

3. SHA-256 integrity

Specification

SHA-256 as defined in NIST FIPS 180-4. Empty-string digest:

e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855

Verification 

f <- tempfile()
file.create(f)
#> [1] TRUE
cer_sha256(f)
#> [1] "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"

Matches the NIST reference.

Summary

Function Formula Verified
cer_safeguard_baseline_trajectory B_t = B_0 * (1 - 0.049)^n Yes
cer_reconcile (V - R) / R Yes
cer_sha256 NIST FIPS 180-4 Yes

Any disagreement between a hand calculation and the package output is a bug; please file an issue.
